title: objectql: uninstalling a base package is refused while its <base>.custom exists, naming the pair (409, the extender-refusal family)
body:
epic:#28130#1 · hotlong · session_040dfd80c4c9411b895c698e785a6848

Filing gate: ④ child of epic #28236 (P1, cut after ADR-0146's rewrite merged in #28295); the epic's two-minute check, verbatim: 「卸载 HotCRM 被拒并点名 `hotcrm.custom`」. ⛔ Not a claim.

Blocked-by: #28404

Part of #28236 (P1, child **N-14**) · governs: ADR-0146 D3 (uninstall bullet) and decided-here item 3, Supersede row ADR-0141 D3 (paired case) · lane: `domain:server` (`packages/objectql`, `packages/metadata-protocol`, `packages/runtime`) · size: S.

**Business reason.** Uninstalling an app while its customizations still exist would strand every override in `hotcrm.custom`. Nothing would serve them and nothing would say why. The administrator is stopped and told which package to export or delete first.

**Measured (`75ecaf4ad8`).**
- `objectql/src/registry.ts#assertPackageUninstallable` (`:5306`) refuses only an owner whose object another package extends, as `PackageUninstallExtendedError` (`:2639`, `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / 409). It is asked by `deletePackage` before its store delete (`metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-uninstall.ts:132`) and by `uninstallPackage` through `unregisterObjectsByPackage`.
- `DELETE /packages/:id` asks `requireWritablePackage(…, 'delete')` first (`runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:2642`). A read-only base (booted code package, marketplace-installed id, scope `system` / `cloud`) is refused `422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` before any uninstall check. At this head that door uninstalls no read-only base at all. The pair check therefore bites on the bases it does uninstall (project-scoped or unmanaged-copied) and on every other caller of `deletePackage` / `uninstallPackage`. Not verified: whether some host removes a managed install by another path.
- No pair check exists anywhere.

**Wanted.**
1. `assertPackageUninstallable(id)` also refuses while the registry holds the pair id of `id` (N-08's constant). Every door that asks it refuses before mutating. The refusal is the same `409` family and envelope, names the pair, and prescribes exporting it (`GET /packages/:id/export` on the pair) or deleting it first. When both causes hold, one refusal carries both.
2. The pair is identified by id, whether the ensure door (N-13) built it or an exported pair was installed. That is why this card does not wait for N-13.
3. On `DELETE /packages/:id` the read-only `422` stays first: it is the truer answer, because even without the pair that door cannot remove the base. The seat measures the two-minute check on the door that uninstalls a base in the test deployment. If no door uninstalls a managed base at this head, it records that on the card ⛔ instead of reordering the gates.
4. Uninstalling the pair itself is unaffected; the `force` path keeps its meaning; the general dependent case (ADR-0141 D3) stays deferred.

**Tests.** New cases in `objectql/src/registry-assert-package-uninstallable.test.ts`: pair present refused naming it; pair absent as before; both causes in one refusal. `packages-uninstall-refuse-before-mutate.test.ts`: with the pair present, the stored row, the registry entry and the disable record are intact.

**Not here.** Creating the pair (N-13); naming constants (N-08); refusing a base upgrade (ADR-0141 D3, deferred); a base removed by redeploying without it (no uninstall door runs).

**Dedupe.** Searched `uninstall dependent`, `uninstall extends refused`, `uninstall protection dependency`: no hit. ADR-0141 D3 deferred the general item by name.

Links back: #28236, ADR-0146 D3, ADR-0141 D3, ADR-0029 (extender refusal).
